correctness.rationale: Restricted-growth canonicalization is a bijection between eight-position equality partitions and ordered word-pair types up to relabeling. The exact exhaustive checker enumerated all Bell(8)=4140 patterns; 3690 satisfy D1-disjointness, the maximum size of the D2-intersection is 4, and the six type signatures are explicit and checkable. Each type with j distinct symbols admits (q)_j injections; one has j=2, four j=3, and one j=4. Direct independent q=2,3,4 enumeration confirmed 2,30,132 ordered pairs. The finite certificate covers the entire all-alphabet structural universe, not a finite sample of alphabets.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The large-n maximum intersection results in Wang–Li–Fu do not characterize n=4, while Sun–Ge general upper bounds neither force maximum four at n=4 nor enumerate all equality-type extremizers. Coverage as a corollary was checked against stated parameter regimes, not inferred from mismatching titles.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Our theorem fixes n=4, s=t=2, enforces D1-disjointness, and classifies every ordered maximum pair with an exact q-polynomial. A bound of at most six for s=t=2 does not entail the sharp four or its extremizers; sufficient-large-n results do not cover n=4. Binary triple-deletion and one-center variance statements have distinct hypotheses and cannot imply the six two-center types.

value.rationale: Complete classification of a natural first finite block-length deletion-reconstruction boundary, including exact optimal intersection, six mutually distinct relabeling types, and their polynomial count over every finite alphabet. It describes the precise change in extremal configurations when alphabets permit 2, 3, or 4 symbols, and is a directly reproducible benchmark for the channel.
